answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit before it can submit a trade, and the market randomly selects one of its past trades for challenge after settlement. If the trade is fabricated or the agent fails to answer, the deposit is slashed and paid to the challenger. Creating a spiral of fake identities therefore requires tying up capital in every account and risking repeated losses; spreading them across an ocean of addresses does not dilute the cost, while a canyon of cheap accounts still cannot make the required deposits free.
